question: ‘National AYUSH Mission’ has been extended up to 31st March 2026. When was the scheme launched?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2014 **__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The National AYUSH Mission (NAM) was launched as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme on 29 September 2014 by the Department of AYUSH, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India during the 12th five year Plan .
 
• It aims to provide cost effective and equitable AYUSH health care throughout the country by improving access to the services.
 
• AYUSH stands for Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy.
 
• The Mission has 4 components:
 
 
• AYUSH Services: Give universal access.
 
• AYUSH Educational Institutions: Strengthen them.
 
• Quality Control of AYUSH Drugs: Set norms and regulate them.
 
• Medicinal Plants: Ensure their supply.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• National AYUSH Mission (NAM) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme that was launched during the 12th Five Year Plan by the Department of AYUSH, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India on 29 September 2014.
 
• The scheme aims to make AYUSH (Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy) healthcare cost-effective, equitable, and easily accessible throughout the country.
